title: Novita AI Pricing: Models & Costs (2026 Guide)
summary: Novita AI pricing uses pay-as-you-go rates for tokens, GPU hours, and serverless seconds, so you can integrate it without committing to a plan.
body_markdown:
## Novita AI vs Together, Fireworks and RunPod


At $1.45, Novita AI has the **lowest H100 hourly rate of the four** , the other three all cost more per hour, making Novita AI the obvious choice for cost-conscious projects. Whether that wins depends on which meter your workload runs on.


It also depends on how many hours the GPU sits idle.


Before comparing rates, read the table, which shows which of the three meters each vendor leads with. A per-token price and a per-hour price can't be set side by side until you know your traffic.


Vendor Meter you pay on Who it suits


Novita AI Tokens, GPU hours, serverless seconds Teams that want to start on tokens and move to rented GPUs later


Together AI Tokens Teams that only call hosted models


Fireworks AI Tokens Teams that only call hosted models


RunPod GPU hours, serverless seconds Teams that already run their own containers


Only Novita AI covers all three meters, so moving between them doesn't mean changing vendor.


### Per-token APIs compared


All three sell hosted open models by the million tokens. Compare the same model, same context length and same input-to-output ratio on each pricing page, since output tokens usually cost more than input.


A chatbot with long replies and a classifier with one-word replies can rank these vendors in opposite orders.


Check rate limits and free credits on each page before you commit; they change often enough that a figure copied into a spreadsheet goes stale quickly.


### GPU rental: Novita AI versus RunPod


On the hourly H100,[Turion's June 2026 comparison](https://turion.ai/blog/gpu-clouds-pricing-comparison-june-2026) puts Novita AI at $3.39 and RunPod at $3.99, meaning RunPod's premium is $0.60 per hour.


Lambda is $4.59, CoreWeave $6.16 and AWS $6.88, with AWS running roughly 50% above Lambda's cost, meaning AWS-dependent organizations pay substantially more than Lambda deployments.


Read Novita's own[bare-metal page](https://novita.ai/gpu-baremetal) as what it is, a vendor's page; it lists the same figures for the four rivals.


$438 a month is the $0.60 gap to RunPod for one GPU left on for 730 hours, showing how hourly differences accumulate over continuous operation, so teams deploying continuous GPU infrastructure should scrutinize hourly rates.


Against AWS the gap is $3.49 an hour, about $2,548 a month.


**An idle GPU still bills at full rate** , so a cheap hour you leave running costs more than an expensive hour you switch off.


### Which one fits which workload


Choose Together AI or Fireworks AI if you only call models and never touch a GPU. Choose Novita AI if your traffic is likely to move between meters, or if steady GPU use makes the lowest hourly rate matter.


> An idle GPU still bills at full rate, so a cheap hour you leave running costs more than an expensive hour you switch off.


Choose RunPod if you bring your own container and want per-second serverless billing for bursts.


**Whichever you pick, set a shutdown schedule first, because idle hours are what separate these vendors' bills most.**
